title: HashSet: How Hash Buckets Guarantee O(1) Lookups
summary: Demystify HashSet internals: how it delegates to an internal HashMap, computes hashCode(), distributes entries into buckets, and checks equals().
learningObjectives: Understand how HashSet delegates internally to a java.util.HashMap
Analyze the PRESENT dummy object pattern used to represent Set element values
Trace hash code spreading and bucket index bitmask calculation
Explain hash collisions, separate chaining, and Java 8 treeification mechanics
expectedOutcomes: Complete technical understanding of why HashSet achieves amortized O(1) performance
Ability to explain bucket calculation and collision resolution in engineering interviews

activities.title: Practical Context: Direct-Mapped Memory Address Translation

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Direct-Mapped Memory Address Translation
analogy.story:
In computer systems hardware, a CPU does not sequentially scan every memory cell when retrieving data from an address. Instead, hardware address decoders compute the exact memory bank and wire line from the address bits in a fraction of a nanosecond.

A hash table functions on the exact same computational philosophy: instead of scanning an entire collection element-by-element, a mathematical hash function maps the element's identity directly to a specific array index (a bucket), reducing lookups from linear O(N) scanning to instantaneous O(1) direct indexing.
analogy.keyTakeaway: HashSet is an abstraction over a hash table. By calculating bucket addresses directly from object hash codes, it replaces costly sequential scans with O(1) direct memory indexing.

activities.title: HashSet Architecture: Internal HashMap Delegation & Hash Buckets

keyTakeaways: HashSet is internally backed by a java.util.HashMap instance
Elements added to a HashSet are stored as KEYS in the internal map; the VALUE is a static dummy Object named PRESENT
Bucket index is calculated via bitwise AND: index = (capacity - 1) & hash(key)
Collisions are resolved via linked list chaining; in Java 8+, chains exceeding TREEIFY_THRESHOLD (8) convert to Red-Black Trees

activities.title: Simulating Hash Buckets and Collision Chains in Java
activities.description: Examine a clear mini-implementation of hash bucket calculation to inspect how objects map to slots and detect collisions.

steps.description: Establish standard capacity of 16 (always a power of 2 in Java HashMap/HashSet).
Apply JDK hash spreading and bitwise AND masking ((CAPACITY - 1) & spreadHash) to constrain the hash to [0, 15] in a single instruction.
Iterate through keys and display how each string's hash code distributes into its respective bucket index.

questions.question: How does java.util.HashSet store elements internally?
options: In an internal Object[] array resized with System.arraycopy
As keys in a private backing HashMap instance, with a dummy Object as the value
In a doubly-linked list of Node pointers
In a native C++ hash register via JNI
questions.explanation: HashSet delegates all storage to a private transient HashMap<E, Object> map. The inserted elements serve as keys, and a static dummy Object named PRESENT serves as the value.

questions.question: Why is the internal capacity of a HashSet always a power of two (e.g., 16, 32, 64)?
options: Because Java memory pages only support powers of two
To permit fast bitwise index calculation (n - 1) & hash instead of expensive modulo division
To prevent the garbage collector from compacting memory
questions.explanation: When capacity n is a power of 2, (n - 1) produces all 1s in binary (e.g. 15 is 01111). The bitwise AND (n - 1) & hash acts as a blazing-fast modulo operation, completing in 1 CPU cycle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the private static final Object PRESENT in HashSet?
options: It acts as a lock object for thread synchronization
It is a placeholder dummy value associated with every key in the internal HashMap
It marks deleted nodes for garbage collection
It stores the maximum capacity of the set
questions.explanation: HashMap requires both a key and a value. Since HashSet only cares about the key, it reuses a single shared dummy Object reference named PRESENT across all map entries to avoid allocating new value objects.

questions.question: What happens in Java 8+ when a single HashSet bucket accumulates 8 or more colliding elements?
options: The colliding linked list is converted into a balanced Red-Black Tree, improving lookup from O(N) to O(log N)
The entire set is immediately discarded and rehashed
New elements for that bucket are rejected
questions.explanation: Java 8 introduced treeification: when a bucket chain length reaches TREEIFY_THRESHOLD (8) and capacity is at least 64, the linked list transforms into a Red-Black Tree to guarantee O(log N) worst-case performance.

questions.question: Explain the relationship between HashSet and HashMap in Java.
questions.answer: HashSet is an architectural wrapper around HashMap. A HashSet instance contains a private transient HashMap<E, Object> field. When set.add(element) is called, HashSet executes map.put(element, PRESENT) where PRESENT is a shared dummy Object. If put() returns null, it signifies the key was new and add() returns true; otherwise it returns false. Similarly, contains() delegates to map.containsKey(), and remove() delegates to map.remove().

questions.question: What is the default initial capacity and load factor of HashSet, and what role do they play?
questions.answer: The default initial capacity is 16 and the default load factor is 0.75. Capacity represents the number of buckets in the underlying hash table. The load factor (0.75) represents the threshold ratio of elements to capacity before resizing occurs (threshold = 16 * 0.75 = 12). When the 13th element is added, the capacity doubles to 32 and all entries are rehashed into the expanded bucket array, maintaining low collision rates.

questions.question: Why is the iteration order of a HashSet non-deterministic?
questions.answer: HashSet iterates over the backing table array sequentially from bucket 0 to capacity - 1. Because an element's bucket index depends on its hashCode() spread against table capacity, objects are placed in pseudo-random bucket slots. When the table resizes, elements are redistributed across new bucket indices, causing iteration order to shift dynamically between resizes.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation: HashSet Internals
checklist: I can describe how HashSet delegates to HashMap and utilizes the PRESENT dummy object
I understand bucket calculation via (capacity - 1) & hash and why power-of-two capacity is critical
I can explain collision resolution mechanisms, including separate chaining and Java 8 treeification

practiceProblems.title: Simulate Bucket Index Calculation
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method computeBucketIndex(int hashCode, int capacity) that returns the bucket index for a given capacity (assumed power of 2) using bitwise masking.
hints: Spread high bits with hash ^ (hash >>> 16) for authentic JDK behavior.

practiceProblems.title: Detect Hash Collisions Between Strings
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of strings and a bucket capacity of 16, count how many strings land in the exact same bucket index as at least one other string.
hints: First pass: tally counts per bucket index.
Second pass: check if the string's bucket has count > 1.

practiceProblems.title: Calculate Threshold and Resize Trigger
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement isResizeNeeded(int currentSize, int capacity, float loadFactor) that returns true if currentSize >= (capacity * loadFactor).

practiceProblems.title: Build a Minimal HashSet Wrapper
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a simple MiniSet<E> backed by an internal HashMap<E, Object> using the dummy PRESENT object pattern.
hints: map.put(key, value) returns null if the key was absent prior to the call.
map.containsKey(key) checks presence in O(1) time.

practiceProblems.title: Find Most Populated Bucket
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of integer values and a hash table capacity of 8, determine the highest number of collisions in any single bucket.
hints: All multiples of 8 will map to bucket index 0 when capacity is 8.
Use an int[] array of size capacity to tally frequencies.
